description:
PRINCIPAL HUNCH (2026-05-29): workflows can ENFORCE disciplines mechanically -- at least the CHECKABLE subset -- rather than relying on prose-in-role-files (soft, forgettable, bloat-prone). A spectrum of enforcement strength:
(i) DETERMINISTIC SCRIPT GATE (no LLM in the gate -- grep/probe/git-state): strongest. e.g. authorship-field grep, pre-branch git checks (PLINY 5.9), voice-leakage grep, cron hygiene.
(ii) SINGLE-DISCIPLINE CHECKER AGENT (focused LLM, one-job-per-agent 4.4 taken to the limit -- one agent, one discipline, no dilution; composable as a parallel fan-out): e.g. 'did this brief CITE the spec line vs re-enumerate from memory?' (ksge D9 / stoa--7b1.6).
(iii) SCHEMA-FORCED VERDICT FIELD (the discipline becomes a required output the agent cannot silently skip; runtime retries until present).
PRINCIPAL named (ii) + (iii); (i) is the strongest form.
PARTITION (the dividing line = last turn's thesis): ENFORCEABLE = syntactic/structural/probe-verifiable disciplines (exactly the ones that bloat prose + get forgotten). NOT ENFORCEABLE = judgment disciplines (direction, taste, novel-attention-surfacing 3) -- stay human/soft, because you can mechanize 'was the discipline followed?' but never 'is this the right direction?'.
EXISTING SEEDS to generalize: CAPTAIN_ZENO (mechanical spec-check = seed of the checker-agent); the verdict schema / save-verdict (seed of the schema-field); the runner skill (probe seed).
TWO PAYOFFS: (a) DEBLOAT lever -- checkable disciplines migrate prose->mechanical, shrinking role files (stoa--xyb) AND making enforcement reliable; (b) serves the direction-is-scarce thesis -- every mechanized discipline is human attention freed for direction.
RISK: who checks the checker? A wrong gate gives false-green (cf. save-verdict /tmp silent-green D5). Deterministic gates > checker-agents on trust. Mechanical enforcement needs its own verification.
NEXT: prototype a single-discipline checker (Mode 2) on ONE checkable discipline, then design which disciplines migrate. N=1; accrete against 6.7.1. Cross-ref: 4.4, CAPTAIN_ZENO, save-verdict, runner skill, stoa--xyb debloat, the thesis, workflow-composer skill.

comments.text:
MODE-2 PROTOTYPE RESULT (run wf_ee8c98f8-04d; 3 single-discipline checker agents, ~10s). Enforced the authorship discipline two ways across 3 samples. Matrix landed as designed:
- S1 clean: tier-i PASS + tier-ii PASS -> GATE PASS. The agent correctly did NOT false-positive on a legit Nate-Jones SOURCE citation (judgment working).
- S2 obvious (author: Nate B. Jones): tier-i FAIL + tier-ii FAIL -> GATE BLOCKED (both caught it).
- S3 subtle (author field clean, but HTML meta + 'Maintained by Jane Famous' in body): tier-i PASS (MISSED) + tier-ii FAIL (caught) -> GATE BLOCKED by agent only. The boundary, demonstrated.

VALIDATED: the hunch holds. Both PRINCIPAL-named mechanisms fired; the deterministic gate (tier i) is the stronger third form. Enforcement = the gate BLOCKS on violation regardless of content quality.

KEY COST FINDING (sharpens the spectrum economics): 3 agent-checks = 102,597 subagent tokens (~34k EACH, fixed overhead even for a trivial check) vs the deterministic gate = 0 tokens (in-script). Practical migration strategy: deterministic gates are the WORKHORSE for reducible disciplines (free, certain, bounded — authorship fields, voice grep, pre-branch git, cron hygiene); reserve tier-ii agent-checkers for the genuinely-judgmental edge (S3-type prose/meta attribution) where a regex cannot reach. N=1; accrete against 6.7.1.

REAL-INCIDENT ANCHOR (N=2): user-beadwork u--ith (threat-defeat verification directive, origindex-trw security drift 2026-05-31) independently arrives at this ticket's tier-iii schema-forced verdict field as its keystone fix (#5: 'mitigation M defeats threat T via probe P'; absence = finding). The discipline-enforcement exploration is now anchored to a production near-miss, not just the authorship teaching demo. Execution home: stoa--ggi (threat-defeat verification hardening epic), child stoa--ggi.1 is the keystone build.

CORRECTION to the prior comment: the threat-defeat execution epic is stoa--yfv (not 'stoa--ggi', which was a typo and does not exist); the keystone build is stoa--yfv.1 (verdict-template threat-coverage assertion = this ticket's tier-iii schema-forced field).
